spatial_claims.claim: C lies on segment AB, between A and B (random cut point)
D lies on extension of AB beyond B, with BD = BC; collinear order is A-C-B-D
AD = AB + BD by segment addition (D beyond B)
B lies between A and D on segment AD (AD cut at B for Prop 2.4)
C lies between A and B on segment AB (AB cut at C for Prop 2.7)
AD is composed of AB and BC as one straight line since BD = BC

configuration_map: All points are collinear in the order A-C-B-D. Point A is the left endpoint of the original segment. Point C is an interior point of AB (the random cut). Point B is the right endpoint of AB and also an interior point of AD. Point D is on the extension of AB beyond B with BD = BC. The entire proof operates on this single line with algebraic identities (Prop 2.4 and 2.7) applied to different cut points on the line.
pass_reason: The proof makes only simple collinear betweenness claims (A-C-B-D ordering) that are all mutually consistent. Prop 2.4 is correctly applied to AD cut at B (B is between A and D), and Prop 2.7 is correctly applied to AB cut at C (C is between A and B). The remaining steps are pure algebraic substitution with no spatial content. No angle decompositions, interior/exterior claims, or circle arguments are involved.
